# Exponential Decay Schedules

## Overview
Exponential decay schedules reduce the learning rate multiplicatively over training steps, providing a smooth, continuous transition from high initial exploration to fine-grained convergence [G]. This family differs from [Linear Learning Rate Schedule](11850-linear-learning-rate-schedule.md) by applying relative reductions rather than absolute ones, and from [Cosine Decay Learning Rate Schedule](14118-cosine-decay-learning-rate-schedule.md) by avoiding the symmetric "slow-fast-slow" trajectory in favor of a monotonic decrease [G]. It is primarily used in NeRF optimization to stabilize training when the model has converged to a coarse geometry but requires precise refinement of appearance and density fields [G].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family compute the learning rate $lr_t$ at step $t$ using a base raised to a power proportional to the normalized step count [G]. The core mechanism is:
$$ lr_t = lr_{initial} \times \gamma^{\frac{t}{T}} $$
where $\gamma$ is the decay factor ($0 < \gamma < 1$) and $T$ is a normalization constant (often total steps or a specific interval) [G]. This ensures the learning rate never reaches zero but asymptotically approaches it [G]. Unlike step decay, there are no discrete jumps [G]. The schedule is often combined with warm-up phases to prevent early instability [G].

## Subtopics

### [Training Loop with Adaptive Regularization & LR Decay](2408-training-loop-with-adaptive-regularization-lr-decay.md)
Defines the standard iterative optimization protocol for NeRFs, combining ray-batched SGD with exponential LR decay and a two-phase loss schedule. It differs from [FreeNeRF](7471-pixelnerf.md) by using simpler auxiliary models for depth supervision rather than annealing positional encoding frequencies, and explicitly manages regularization weights that decay alongside the learning rate. Choose it for sparse input scenarios requiring explicit regularization management.

### [Exponential Decay Learning Rate Schedule](9145-exponential-decay-learning-rate-schedule.md)
Applies a base raised to a normalized step exponent to transition from an initial to a final value. It differs from [Linear Learning Rate Schedule](11850-linear-learning-rate-schedule.md) by applying multiplicative reductions rather than additive ones, and from [Cosine Decay Learning Rate Schedule](14118-cosine-decay-learning-rate-schedule.md) by providing a continuous curve rather than a symmetric decay profile. Choose it when a monotonic, framework-agnostic decay is required.

### [Exponential Decay Learning Rate Schedule with Warm-up](14980-exponential-decay-learning-rate-schedule-with-warm-up.md)
Combines a linear warm-up phase with an exponential decay trajectory, specifically targeting per-camera exposure parameters or main network weights. It distinguishes itself from [Cosine Decay Learning Rate Schedule](14118-cosine-decay-learning-rate-schedule.md) by using a constant rate during warm-up followed by geometric decay, and from [Exponential Decay Learning Rate Schedule](9145-exponential-decay-learning-rate-schedule.md) by explicitly incorporating a delayed warm-up period to stabilize initial training. Choose it for sparse or complex captures to prevent large gradient updates before geometric priors are established.

## Background
Exponential decay is a standard technique in optimization, widely adopted in early neural network training and retained in NeRF pipelines for its simplicity and effectiveness in fine-tuning [G]. In the context of differentiable volume rendering, it addresses the problem of converging sparse input data by preventing large gradient updates once the model has established a coherent geometric prior [G].
